Mark anything you could not verify from a primary or official source as UNVERIFIED rather than guessing.

1. WSA velocity relation: (a) the original Arge et al. 2003 (AIP Conf. Proc. 679, 190) and Arge et al. 2004 (JASTP 66, 1295) forms and coefficients; (b) McGregor et al. 2011 (JGR 116, A03101) form; (c) Riley et al. 2015 (Space Weather 13, 154) form/coefficients used for comparison; (d) Reiss et al. 2019 (ApJS 240, 35) and Reiss et al. 2020 (ApJ 891, 165) — what coefficients/optimizations they report; (e) the form used in WSA v5.x at CCMC/iSWA (one header we found reads VELEQN = '285.0+625.0/((1.0 + fexp)**(0.22222)) * (1.0 - 0.8*exp(-(arc_ft_bd/2.0)**2.0))**3.0' km/s at 21.5 Rs — confirm any published description of WSA v5.x/v4.x coefficients, e.g., in Wallace et al. 2020 Solar Phys, Arge's group papers, or CCMC model pages).
2. ENLIL inner boundary at 21.5 Rs (0.1 AU) for the CCMC "a6b1" ambient setting: defaults for vfast, vslow, vrfast/vrslow (velocity reductions, e.g. 75 km/s), dfast (fast-stream density, e.g. 125 or 300 cm^-3?), tfast (e.g. 0.8 MK), bfast/bscl, xalpha (alpha fraction 0.05?), and the rules: density n v^2 = const or n ∝ v^-2 (momentum-flux balance), temperature from thermal-pressure balance n T = const, Br from WSA scaled. Sources: Odstrcil 2003 (Adv. Space Res. 32, 497), Odstrcil et al. 2004 (JASTP 66, 1311), Mays et al. 2015 (Solar Phys 290, 1775), Jian et al. 2015/2016 (Space Weather), CCMC ENLIL documentation pages (ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/models/ENLIL~2.8f or similar), and "Wold et al. 2018 (JSWSC)" or "Wold 2018". Also the "g53q5" runpar meaning (gamma=5/3? heating?). And cone-cloud defaults "d4t1x1" (density 4x fast wind, temperature 1x, elongation 1).
3. EUHFORIA inner boundary (Pomoell & Poedts 2018, J. Space Weather Space Clim. 8, A35): the exact velocity formula (240 + 675/(1+f)^0.222 [1 − 0.8 exp(−(d/w)^β)]^3?), w and β values, the 50 km/s reduction and 675 km/s cap, n = n_fsw (v_fsw/v)^2 with n_fsw, v_fsw, T_fsw, B_fsw values, and the B_r prescription. Also note any later EUHFORIA updates (e.g., Samara et al. 2021/2024, Asvestari et al.).
4. BRaVDA / HUXt data assimilation: Lang & Owens 2019 (Space Weather 17, 59) and Lang et al. 2021 (Space Weather 19, e2020SW002698): what is assimilated, typical improvement, and whether STEREO-A in-situ data are used.
5. Status/availability in Nov–Dec 2025 of: PUNCH (launched March 2025; science data release status and URL), STEREO-A HI-1/HI-2 (beacon vs science data, UKSSDC/STEREO SSC URLs), LOFAR IPS (Space weather campaigns; LOFAR2.0 upgrade downtime in 2024-2026?), CACTus (sidc.be/cactus, does it cover Nov 2025 with LASCO and/or STEREO-A COR2?), SOHO/LASCO CDAW catalog (cdaw.gsfc.nasa.gov/CME_list — latest month covered), GOES-19 CCOR-1 operational status.
6. Coronal-hole products usable as WSA checks for Nov 2025: e.g., CATCH, CHIMERA (solarmonitor), SPoCA/CHIMERA via HEK, NOAA SWPC coronal-hole maps, and STEREO-A EUVI synoptic maps; give URLs.

Web search results for query: "Pomoell Poedts 2018 EUHFORIA inner boundary velocity 240 675 (1+f)^0.222 0.8 exp w β"

Links: [{"title":"Implementing the MULTI-VP coronal model in EUHFORIA: test case results and comparisons with the WSA coronal model","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.06617"},{"title":"Calibrating the WSA model in EUHFORIA based on PSP observations","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.09693"},{"title":"MHD simulations on the large-scale propagation of high-speed solar wind streams","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.01613"},{"title":"Modelling a multi-spacecraft coronal mass ejection encounter with EUHFORIA","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.11831"},{"title":"Testing the background solar wind modelled by EUHFORIA","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.07461"},{"title":"Exploring the radial evolution of Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections using EUHFORIA","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.07569"},{"title":"Implementation and validation of the FRi3D flux rope model in EUHFORIA","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2207.06707"},{"title":"Calibrating the WSA model in EUHFORIA based on PSP observations","url":"https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.09693"},{"title":"EGU22 8932","url":"https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EGU22/EGU22-8932.html"}]

The search confirmed the formula and default constants, which come from multiple EUHFORIA papers citing Pomoell & Poedts (2018).

- **Formula:** One paper gives the inner-boundary radial speed as a base speed V0 plus a term scaled by the flux-tube expansion factor f raised to a power, multiplied by a bracketed correction involving 0.8, an exponential of the footpoint angular distance d over w, and an exponent β, cubed. (The radial velocity is provided by the WSA model based on the following equation, with the 0.8 exponential term inside the bracket.)
- **Default constants:** Several sources list V0 = 240 km/s, V1 = 675 km/s, α = 0.222, and w = 0.02 rad. One paper also gives β = 1.25 (see Pomoell & Poedts 2018, for more details). Another paper uses the same values for these constants (v0 = 240 km s-1, v1 = 675 km s-1, α = 0.222, β = 1.25 and w = 0.02 rad).
- **Expansion factor:** f is defined from the photospheric and 0.1 au radial magnetic fields, with the inner boundary at 0.1 au (R_b = 0.1 au).
- **Caveat on the EUHFORIA version:** One 2024 paper notes that the version of WSA in EUHFORIA is different from the original WSA model (see differences between Pomoell & Poedts 2018 and Arge et al. 2003, 2004). A 2019 paper also says it subtracts 50 km/s and clamps speeds to 275–625 km/s, so those are user-applied modifications rather than part of the base formula.

I did not retrieve the original Pomoell & Poedts (2018) paper itself, so the constants above are as reported by secondary sources.

Multi-point Validation in the Inner Heliosphere","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.22386"},{"title":"Wang%E2%80%93Sheeley%E2%80%93Arge model","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang%E2%80%93Sheeley%E2%80%93Arge_model"},{"title":"Forecasting the Ambient Solar Wind with Numerical Models: I. On the Implementation of an Operational Framework","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.04353"},{"title":"SWASTi-SW: Space Weather Adaptive SimulaTion framework for Solar Wind and its relevance to ADITYA-L1 mission","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2207.13708"},{"title":"Impact of Non-potential Coronal Boundary Conditions on Solar Wind Prediction","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01730"},{"title":"riley wsa sw v4","url":"https://www.predsci.com/~pete/research/wsa-sw-manuscript/riley-wsa-sw-v4.pdf"},{"title":"odstrcil ccmc2012","url":"https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/publicData/workshops/2012/Monday_pdf/odstrcil_ccmc2012.pdf"},{"title":"www.spaceweather.gov","url":"https://www.spaceweather.gov/node/42"},{"title":"agu.confex.com","url":"https://agu.confex.com/agu/fm15/webprogram/Paper69503.html"}]

I ran one search. It did not surface the Riley 2015 *Space Weather* paper on inner heliosphere models, and it did not confirm the 285/625 coefficients.

- **Wrong-journal lead:** The closest Riley 2015 match is a draft titled "On the Role Played by Magnetic Expansion Factor in the Prediction of Solar Wind Speed," by Riley, Linker, and Arge, dated January 2015. It is marked for the *Journal of Geophysical Research*, not *Space Weather*. The WSA model has evolved so much that the role played by the expansion factor term is now largely minimal, being supplanted by the distance from the coronal hole boundary (DCHB). You may be thinking of a different paper.
- **Formula check:** An adapted WSA implementation (SWASTi-SW) writes the speed as a minimum speed plus a maximum speed divided by (1+f_s)^(2/9), multiplied by a bracketed term that includes an exponential in (d/w)^β. That bracketed term has a 0.8 coefficient and a cube, which your query omits. Though there are many different forms of WSA solar wind relations, in SWASTi-SW we have used the following, so the exact form depends on the implementation.
- **Parameter sources:** A more general WSA form uses eight free parameters, including fast and slow wind speeds, so 285 and 625 km/s are plausibly the slow and fast speeds. There are eight free parameters, including the fast and slow wind speed v_fast and v_slow. I could not verify that these particular values come from Riley 2015.
- **Context:** A 2025 arXiv paper notes that the current version of the WSA model was originally optimized for near-Earth observations.

To pin down the source, search for the exact title of the Riley 2015 *Space Weather* paper or its DOI.

The search didn't turn up an arXiv entry for the 2018 Pomoell and Poedts paper itself. The published version is in *Space Weather and Space Climate*, volume 8 (2018), article A35, DOI 10.1051/swsc/2018020, with 14 pages. The journal listing gives the title and says the paper covers the model's implementation and first results.

The paper describes EUHFORIA as having two main parts, a coronal model and a heliosphere model that includes coronal mass ejections. The heliosphere part is a magnetohydrodynamic model of the inner heliosphere, and semi-empirical methods supply its boundary conditions. Later papers cite the 2018 paper as the reference for EUHFORIA's 3D MHD equations, and the arXiv results include two follow-up studies that use the model. Hinterreiter et al. (arXiv:1907.07461, 2019) assess its background solar wind output against ACE data.

**Inner boundary conditions (EUHFORIA 1.0.4 default setup)**

- **WSA velocity formula (Eq. 1):** v(f,d) = v0 + v1/(1+f)^α · [1 − 0.8·exp(−(d/w)^β)]^3, where f is the flux tube expansion factor and d is the angular distance to the nearest coronal hole boundary.
- **Constants:** v0 = 240 km/s, v1 = 675 km/s, α = 0.222, β = 1.25, w = 0.02 rad.
- **Speed adjustment:** The paper subtracts 50 km/s, stating it was done "to avoid a systematic overestimate of the wind speed." The speed map is also rotated by 10°.
- **Speed clamp:** Minimum 275 km/s and maximum 625 km/s.
- **Density (Eq. 2):** n = n_fsw (v_fsw / v_r)^2, with n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³ and v_fsw = 675 km/s. Here v_r is the empirical speed.
- **Temperature:** No explicit temperature rule is given. The paper instead sets a constant thermal pressure of 3.3 nPa at the inner boundary, which it describes as consistent with a fast wind temperature of about 0.8 MK.
- **Magnetic field:** The field topology comes from the Schatten current sheet (SCS) model. The field magnitude is proportional to speed, with B_fsw = 300 nT at v_fsw = 675 km/s. The paper does not specify how the sign of B_r is determined from the PFSS solution.
- **Attribution to Pomoell & Poedts (2018):** The WSA-based speed relation is attributed to them (Eq. 2 in their paper), and the density relation is attributed to them as well (Eq. 4 in their paper).

**Paper details**

- **Authors:** Jürgen Hinterreiter, Jasmina Magdalenic, Manuela Temmer, Christine Verbeke, Immanuel Christopher Jebaraj, Evangelia Samara, Eleanna Asvestari, Stefaan Poedts, Jens Pomoell, Emilia Kilpua, Luciano Rodriguez, Camilla Scolini, and Alexey Isavnin.
- **Journal:** Not stated in the provided content.
- **Year:** Not stated in the provided content. The arXiv identifier (1907.07461) points to July 2019.

**WSA formula (default in EUHFORIA)**

v_r(f, d) = V0 + V1 / (1 + f)^α × [1 − 0.8·exp(−(d/w)^β)]³

- **Default constants:** V0 = 240 km/s, V1 = 675 km/s, α = 0.222, β = 1.25, w = 0.02 rad.
- **Flux-tube expansion (f):** the paper revises the reference radius to R_b = 2.5 R☉ (instead of 0.1 au).

**Ad hoc rules at 0.1 au**

- **Speed adjustment:** 50 km/s is subtracted from the velocities at 0.1 au to offset MHD acceleration in the heliospheric model.
- **Speed caps:** velocities at 0.1 au are limited to the range 275 to 625 km/s.

**Density, temperature/pressure, and magnetic field at 0.1 au**

- **Density:** n = n_fsw·(v_fsw/v_r)², with n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³.
- **Temperature:** T = T_fsw·(ρ_fsw/ρ), with T_fsw = 0.8 MK. The thermal pressure is held constant at the boundary at 3.3 nPa.
- **Mass density:** ρ_fsw = 0.5·n_fsw·m_p.
- **Radial field:** B_r = sgn(B_corona)·B_fsw·(v_r/v_fsw), with B_fsw = 300 nT and v_fsw = 675 km/s.

**PSP-calibrated constants proposed in the paper**

- **V0:** 207 km/s (default 240).
- **V1:** 725 km/s (default 675).
- **w and β:** the paper's best PSP-matching pair is w = 0.031 rad with β = 0.50. The runner-ups are (0.035 rad, 0.50) and (0.026 rad, 0.50).
- **Caveat:** these PSP-matched settings gave poorer predictions at Earth than the default setup. The paper concludes the WSA relation may need a broader reformulation.

**Bibliographic details**

- **Title:** Calibrating the WSA model in EUHFORIA based on PSP observations
- **Authors:** E. Samara, C. N. Arge, R. F. Pinto, J. Magdalenić, N. Wijsen, M. L. Stevens, L. Rodriguez, S. Poedts
- **Year:** 2024 (arXiv:2405.09693v1, submitted 15 May 2024)
- **Journal:** not stated on the page
- **DOI:** not provided on the page

Links: [{"title":"On the Relationship between Magnetic Expansion Factor and Observed Speed of the Solar Wind from Coronal Pseudostreamers","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.16168"},{"title":"Influence of Non-Potential Coronal Magnetic Topology on Solar-Wind Models","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.00427"},{"title":"research.ssl.berkeley.edu","url":"https://research.ssl.berkeley.edu/cism/papers/Arge03.pdf"},{"title":"Number of the records: 1","url":"https://asep.lib.cas.cz/arl-cav/en/detail-cav_un_epca-0125225-Improved-method-for-specifying-solar-wind-speed-near-the-Sun"},{"title":"Improved method for specifying solar wind speed near the Sun","url":"https://experts.colorado.edu/display/pubid_112176"},{"title":"Počet záznamů: 1","url":"https://asep.lib.cas.cz/arl-cav/cs/detail-cav_un_epca-0125225-Improved-method-for-specifying-solar-wind-speed-near-the-Sun"},{"title":"Improved method for specifying solar wind speed near the Sun","url":"https://vivo.colorado.edu/display/pubid_112176"},{"title":"www.spaceweather.ac.cn","url":"https://www.spaceweather.ac.cn/~fshen/474-0172.pdf"},{"title":"riley unipolar streamers","url":"https://www.predsci.com/%7Epete/research/luhmann/revision-3/riley-unipolar-streamers.bbl"},{"title":"www.spaceweather.ac.cn","url":"https://www.spaceweather.ac.cn/~fshen/JASTP2012.pdf"}]

The search confirmed the paper's bibliographic details but did not return its formula, so I can't verify the "265" constant from these results.

- **Citation:** The paper is Arge, Odstrčil, Pizzo & Mayer, "Improved method for specifying solar wind speed near the Sun," in *Solar Wind Ten* (AIP Conf. Proc. 679, pp. 190–193). It was presented at the 10th International Solar Wind Conference, with a publication date of June 17, 2002 (the proceedings volume is dated 2003). Sources: Arge et al. (2003), Odstrcil, Pizzo, Mayer: Improved method for specifying solar wind speed near the sun in the Riley bibliography, and the CU Experts record.
- **Method:** The paper's core idea is that the wind speed near the Sun depends on the magnetic expansion factor plus the minimum angular distance from an open-field footpoint to the nearest coronal hole boundary. The authors used three linked coronal and solar wind models and polar-field-corrected Mount Wilson Carrington maps from 1995 (CU/Berkeley PDF, index 3-3 and 3-4 context).
- **Formula:** A later version of the formula appears in a 2015 arXiv paper (arXiv 1511.00427). It gives v = 240 + 675/(1+f_s)^(1/4.5) × [1 − 0.8·exp(−(θ_b/1.9)²)]³ km/s and is described as a slight modification of the Arge et al. (2004) formula. That version uses 240 and 675, not 265, so the 265 constant likely comes from the 2003 paper or a different version. I could not confirm it.

To check the 265 value, the Berkeley PDF (research.ssl.berkeley.edu/cism/papers/Arge03.pdf) is the most direct source; the search returned only its first pages.

The search didn't confirm the exact 240/675 values or the McGregor 2011 A03101 formula, so I can't verify your parameter set against that paper.

What I did find:

- **Parameter set in a 2025 arXiv paper:** That paper uses V_min = 250, V_max = 750, α = 0.222 (which matches 1/4.5), β = 1.25, w = 0.028, a1 = 0.8, and a2 = 3. It cites McGregor et al. 2011 and others as the source of these values, consistent with previous studies. This is the closest match to your query, but it is not the same as 240/675.
- **Paper identification:** The A03101 article is McGregor, Hughes, Arge, Owens and Odstrcil (2011), "The distribution of solar wind speeds during solar minimum," Journal of Geophysical Research, 116, A03101, doi 10.1029/2010JA015881. Its abstract says the new relationship was tested by driving the ENLIL 3-D MHD model.
- **Other calibrations:** A separate 2025 arXiv paper lists V0 = 285 km/s, V1 = 625 km/s, α = 0.222, β = 2 and w = 2 rad, which is a different set. It also says McGregor et al. (2011) calibrated the relation against Helios data.

To confirm the 240/675 values, check the published A03101 paper directly (doi 10.1029/2010JA015881), since the search results didn't include its equations.

The search did not turn up the Arge et al. (2003) paper itself, and none of the results list the constants 265, 5.8, 1.6, or 7.5, so I can't confirm those values from it.

What the results do show:

- **The general form.** One paper gives the WSA formula as the slow-wind speed plus the fast-minus-slow difference divided by (1 + f_s) raised to a power α, times a bracketed θ_b term raised to a further power. The bracket contains β, γ, an exponential in (θ_b/ω)^δ, and eight free parameters in total ([1-3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01730)). That paper also says the WSA model is the one used operationally at NOAA SWPC, citing Arge et al. (2003) ([1-1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01730)).
- **A specific variant.** A different study uses a version with fixed constants of 0.8 inside the exponential and an exponent of 3.5 on the bracket ([2-4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.13793)). Its θ_b is the minimum angular distance from a coronal hole boundary ([2-5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.13793)).
- **Where θ_b saturates.** One paper reports that the empirical speed often stops depending on θ_b once θ_b is roughly 7° or more ([5-3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1303.0563)). That may be related to the 7.5 in your query, but I haven't verified it.

To pin down the exact constants, the original Arge et al. (2003) proceedings in *Solar Wind Ten* (AIP Conf. Proc. 679, pp. 190–193, doi 10.1063/1.1618574) would need to be checked directly. Its bibliographic details appear in [3-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.16279) and [7-1](https://vivo.colorado.edu/display/pubid_112176). Other papers may use different constants, so the values should be matched to the specific paper you're working from.
